topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: Prerequisites: Neurons as Knowledge Keys
lecture_lines: MLPs function as key-value retrieval systems.
animations: Show MLP architecture block (#FF5733) representing input and retrieval with [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/key.svg].
Display linear transformation arrow (#33FF57) moving through neuron layers using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/neuron.svg].
Animate non-linear activation function (#3357FF) highlighting active pathways using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/filter.svg].

sections.title: The Mechanism: Pattern Matching
lecture_lines: Specific neurons act as knowledge keys.
They trigger when encountering specific patterns.
animations: Display a specific neuron [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/neuron.svg] key icon (#FFFF33) in the layer.
Animate the input pattern (#FF33FF) overlapping with the neuron [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/neuron.svg] key.
Display a connection using the key [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/key.svg] (#00FFFF) confirming accurate knowledge retrieval.

sections.title: Conceptualizing Memory: The Weights as a Database
lecture_lines: Layer one weights store the key.
Layer two weights store the value.
The system triggers a specific fact.
It outputs the desired retrieved word.
animations: Show grid of weights (#CCCCCC) resembling a database table [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/table.svg].
Highlight the first weight layer (#FF5733) storing the key pattern [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/database.svg].
Highlight the second weight layer (#33FF57) storing the value facts [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/database.svg].
Animate a triggering mechanism (#FFFF33) lighting up the specific fact row [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/table.svg].
Display the retrieved word output (#FFFFFF) in a final bubble [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bubble.svg].

sections.title: Integration: Why MLPs vs. Attention?
lecture_lines: Attention coordinates; MLPs hold the knowledge.
animations: Show attention mechanism (#FF5733) connecting different token nodes represented by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/brain.svg].
Show MLP storage (#33FF57) as a dense block of memory using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/filing.svg].
Animate attention routing signals (#FFFFFF) vs MLP memory activation (#FFFF33) retrieved from [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/library.svg].

sections.title: Summary & Visual Conclusion
lecture_lines: MLPs match input patterns to facts.
Activation triggers the stored fact storage.
Facts are retrieved through neuron firing.
animations: Show input pattern [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/brain.svg] (#FF33FF) approaching the MLP structure.
Animate the firing of a specific neuron (#FFFF33) upon pattern match.
Display the retrieved fact text (#00FFFF) emerging from the output.
